title: Trigonometric Integrals
summary: Integrals of powers of sine, cosine, tangent, and secant use trig identities to reduce to substitutions. Odd powers peel off one factor for $u$-substitution; even powers use the power-reduction (half-angle) identities.

power-reduction.plain: Identities that lower even powers of sin/cos.

odd power trick.plain: Peel one factor to pair with $du$.
odd power trick.in_class: Save one $\sin$ (or $\cos$) and convert the rest with $\sin^2+\cos^2=1$.

secant-tangent.in_class: Save a $\sec\tan$ or $\sec^2$ for the substitution.

u = sin or cos.plain: The substitution after peeling a factor.
u = sin or cos.in_class: Choose so its derivative matches the saved factor.

product to sum.plain: Rewriting $\sin A\cos B$ etc. as sums.

reduce then integrate.in_class: Turn powers into manageable single terms.

concept_sections.heading: Odd powers of sine or cosine
concept_sections.explanation: If one of them has an odd power, save a single factor for $du$ and convert the remaining even power with $\sin^2+\cos^2=1$, then substitute.

figure.caption: Odd powers of sine or cosine

concept_sections.heading: Even powers
concept_sections.explanation: When both powers are even, use power-reduction: $\sin^2 x=\tfrac{1-\cos2x}{2}$, $\cos^2 x=\tfrac{1+\cos2x}{2}$. This lowers the degree until integration is direct.

concept_sections.heading: Tangent and secant
concept_sections.explanation: For $\int\sec^m\tan^n$, if $\sec$ has an even power save $\sec^2$ ($=du$ for $u=\tan$); if $\tan$ has an odd power save $\sec\tan$ ($=du$ for $u=\sec$). Use $1+\tan^2=\sec^2$ to convert.

concept_sections.heading: Products of different angles
concept_sections.explanation: For $\int\sin(mx)\cos(nx)\,dx$ use product-to-sum identities to turn the product into a sum of single trig terms, then integrate.

concept_sections.heading: Choosing the method
concept_sections.explanation: Scan the powers: any odd power ⇒ peel a factor; all even ⇒ power-reduce; sec/tan ⇒ pick $u=\tan$ or $u=\sec$. A quick classification saves work.
